3.1 — The Turret: Distance & the Detection Radius

Until now, the world has been passive: coins wait to be collected and spikes wait to be bumped. The Turret is your first adversary that decides. Before it can shoot, it must be aware. Today, you break enemy awareness into smaller sub-problems, read Unity's spatial functions, and build TurretController.cs from scratch.

Read the Docs ~15 min

Building artificial intelligence starts with breaking down awareness into smaller questions:

  1. Who is my target and where are they? (Target acquisition)
  2. How far away is the target right now? (Distance measurement)
  3. Is the target inside my danger zone? (Selection condition)

Socratic: Comparing Targeting & Distance Functions

Sub-problem 1: Locating the Target. Compare these two Unity techniques:

ApproachExamplePros & Cons
GameObject.FindWithTagGameObject.FindWithTag("Player")Searches the entire scene by tag. Very flexible, but scanning all scene objects is slow if called repeatedly in Update().
[SerializeField] reference[SerializeField] private Transform playerTransform;Directly linked in the Inspector. Zero search time, but requires manual wiring and fails if targets spawn dynamically at runtime.

Sub-problem 2: Measuring Distance. Compare these two math approaches:

FunctionExamplePerformance Note
Vector3.DistanceVector3.Distance(posA, posB)Calculates the exact Euclidean distance ((\sqrt{Delta x^2 + Delta y^2})). Clean and readable.
sqrMagnitude(posB - posA).sqrMagnitude <= range * rangeCompares squared distances. Skips the square root operation entirely, saving massive CPU power when hundreds of enemies search at once!
  1. If you use GameObject.FindWithTag, why should it be called once in Start() and stored in a variable (cached), rather than called 60 times a second in Update()?
  2. In what scenarios would you choose Vector3.Distance, and in what scenarios is sqrMagnitude preferred?
Read Function-Level Examples ~15 min

Notice how each targeting and distance function works in isolation across completely different systems:

Example 1 — Caching a Tagged Object on a Rescue Helicopter:

// Searches the scene hierarchy once during initialization to locate a tagged target
GameObject beaconObject = GameObject.FindWithTag("EmergencyBeacon");
if (beaconObject != null)
{
    beaconTransform = beaconObject.transform;
}

Example 2 — Measuring Euclidean Distance on a Museum Laser Tripwire:

// Calculates straight-line distance between two 3D points
float intruderDistance = Vector3.Distance(laserEmitter.position, intruderTransform.position);
if (intruderDistance <= alertRadius)
{
    Debug.Log("Laser beam broken! Intruder distance: " + intruderDistance);
}

Example 3 — High-Performance Distance with sqrMagnitude:

// Avoids the computationally expensive square-root operation (ideal for hundreds of particles)
float sqrDist = (particleA.position - particleB.position).sqrMagnitude;
if (sqrDist <= activationRadius * activationRadius)
{
    // Proximity triggered without invoking Mathf.Sqrt
}

Predict Before Building

  1. Why is calling GameObject.FindWithTag() once in Start() considered good engineering, while calling it inside Update() causes frame-rate drops?
  2. In Example 2, what would happen if intruderTransform was null when calling Vector3.Distance? What guard clause should always precede distance checks?
Build Lab: Your Turn ~25 min
Architectural Specification for TurretController.cs:

Detection Range Knob:

  • Where in Assets/Scripts/ should you create this script, and what must the class name match?
  • What serialized variable allows level designers to adjust how far the turret can see from the Inspector? What should its default float value be?

Tracking the Target:

  • What component on a GameObject holds its 2D/3D coordinates in world space?
  • How can you store a cached reference to the Player's transform?
  • Why should you find and cache the player reference once in Start() rather than searching for it every frame in Update()?
  • What function finds an object in the scene by its tag? What tag does the Player have?
  • What safety check should you perform if FindWithTag fails to find any matching object?

Evaluating Distance in Update:

  • If the player reference hasn't been found (or is null), what guard clause should prevent the rest of Update() from running?
  • How do you measure the Euclidean distance between the turret's position and the player's position?
  • What condition checks if the player has entered the turret's danger zone?
  • When the player is within range, how do you log a diagnostic message confirming detection?

Step 2 — Attach to the Turret in Unity.

  1. Open the Overworld scene and select the Turret GameObject.
  2. Click Add Component and choose Turret Controller.
  3. Notice the Max Attack Range field in the Inspector defaults to 7.

Step 3 — Test the boundary live. Press Play. Walk your player toward the turret while watching the Console:

  • At distance 7.1: The Console is quiet.
  • At distance 6.9: The Console repeatedly logs Player in range!.
  • Walk away past 7: The messages stop.

Bug Hunt: Testing Range Conditions

  1. What happens if you temporarily change the Player's tag to Untagged and press Play? What error message appears in the Console, and why?
  2. In TurretController.cs, what is the difference between <= maxAttackRange and < maxAttackRange? At what exact distance value would the behavior differ?
  3. In the Inspector, change Max Attack Range to 2. Walk around the turret. How does changing this single knob transform the turret from a sniper into a close-quarters sentry?
Tinker ~10 min

Tinker: Visualizing the Aggro Zone

  1. Add this Unity built-in function to the bottom of TurretController.cs: 
    private void OnDrawGizmosSelected()
{
    Gizmos.color = Color.red;
    Gizmos.DrawWireSphere(transform.position, maxAttackRange);
}
    Select the Turret in the Scene view. What does Unity draw, and why is this tool invaluable for game designers?
  2. Tune maxAttackRange: What radius feels challenging without being frustrating? Write down your preferred number and explain your reasoning.

Checkpoint — before moving on, you must be able to:

  • Break down autonomous entity awareness into target acquisition and distance testing
  • Explain why caching references in Start() is superior to calling FindWithTag in Update()
  • Use Vector3.Distance inside an if condition
  • Create TurretController.cs and attach it to a scene GameObject
  • Commit your detection radius code to GitHub
